sessions.label: turn-3
replies:
The guide says you'll need:

- A 5 mm hex key for the mounting bolt
- A clean-cutting cable cutter (so the cable doesn't fray)
- A chain tool or quick-link pliers
- A Phillips screwdriver for the limit screws
- A little grease for the bolt threads

It also suggests a bike stand, or turning the bike upside down on a soft mat. Tighten the new derailleur to the torque printed on its body, usually 8 to 10 Nm, and check the hanger is straight first.

The page repeats the same steps four times, so it's probably a glitch in the page rather than four different guides.

sessions.label: turn-4
replies: Good plan. A chain tool is the one tool you can't skip for this job, so it's worth borrowing. Ask Tomas whether he also has a 5 mm hex key and a cable cutter, since you'll need those too.

replies: Tonight, try a quick chickpea and spinach pasta: cook the pasta, then sauté garlic, a can of drained chickpeas and a handful of spinach in olive oil with a squeeze of lemon. Finish with the pasta water, a little grated hard cheese, and black pepper. It's mild, uses no cashews, and takes about 25 minutes. Cook the garlic gently and skip raw onion.

sessions.label: turn-9

The 09:15 from Porto São Bento is the one. It reaches Régua at 11:12, which is just after 11:00, so it doesn't meet your deadline. The 07:25 arrives at 09:20 but doesn't run on weekends. The 08:05 weekend departure arrives at 10:02, so that's the one to take if you travel on a weekend.

On weekdays, the 07:25 is your only option before 11:00. Those times are from the timetable page and may change, so check for engineering works before you travel. Bikes go free on regional trains when there's space, up to two per carriage.
